aggregation: Equal weights, 0.2 per dimension; rubric specifies no other weights. Scores are judgment, not probabilities or test pass rates.
reasoning: The bounded safety/dictation implementation is acceptable. The full spoken editing experience is not accepted: the final-image synthetic ASR run still fails four of nine commands, and physical-microphone accuracy and speech-end-to-visible latency are unaccepted. Passing execution tests cannot override that gate.

scoped_implementation.scope: VOICE-QUALITY-V3 PM acceptance: editor safety, dictation, bounded execution, transport compatibility, preservation constraints and honest ASR evaluation contract

score_reasons.correctness: Capture context survives the queue; deletion and dictation validate revision and slide identity under the document lock; expiry cancels dependent commands. Reviewed fixes and regression cases support correctness, without proving every browser schedule.
score_reasons.completeness: All nine bounded acceptance topics are addressed. The ASR requirement is an honest evaluation contract, not an ASR quality win. Physical voice acceptance and parity of multi-utterance dictation in the second editor remain outside demonstrated completion.
score_reasons.idiomatic: Uses existing React hooks, queue, transport, FastAPI schemas, edit locks and persistence paths; the evaluator reuses the production parser and PCM transport.
score_reasons.maintainability: Small context/dictation/preservation helpers and explicit limits keep the change scoped. Dense EditPage lifecycle logic and a bespoke mocked React scheduler prevent an excellent score.
score_reasons.test_coverage: Strong negative, concurrency, persistence/undo and transport coverage, including 11 persisted integration-style cases. React scheduling/devices/server boundaries are mocked; skipped tests and absent physical-microphone/browser lifecycle acceptance preclude 5/5.

strengths: Four reviewer races are closed in review.md; corresponding production guards and 11 integration-style cases were inspected. The verifier's capture-gap regression is also retained.
Stale/conflicting dictation and deletion reject before mutation; dictation has one persistence transaction and undo coverage.
Flush, acknowledgement and server finalization have bounded waits; forced stop and session invalidation take precedence.
Evidence distinguishes parser/execution, local-model latency, Live pipeline continuity, synthetic recognition and physical microphone acceptance.
weaknesses: Synthetic ASR remains FAIL 5/9 on the final image; select, move, replace and append fail. This is an unchanged release blocker.
No accepted human microphone/noise corpus or speech-end-to-visible latency distribution. One warm model sample is not p95 or end-to-end voice latency.
Number/date preservation is a conservative lexical check, not semantic equivalence or comprehensive support for spelled-out values.
Full Python regression remains non-green: 9/871 failures, reported identically reproduced on clean base. This judge did not independently repeat that comparison.
Native decoder process isolation, advanced semantic groups/layout and second-editor dictation parity are not delivered claims.
